Founded in 1998, it facilitates digital payments through [[Android (operating system)|Android]]-based POS machines that are primarily used by retailers in India, [[UAE]], and [[Malaysia]].{{cite news |title=Here are the top 10 highest-funded startups in India |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/photos/startup/oyo-byjus-among-the-top-funded-startups-in-india-3503811-2.htm |publisher=[[CNBC TV18]] |date=29 May 2019|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{cite news |last1=Gooptu |first1=Biswarup |last2=Bhakta |first2=Pratik |title=Season may be right for Sequoia to exit Pine Labs |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/season-may-be-right-for-sequoia-to-exit-pine-labs/articleshow/60251923.cms |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=28 August 2017|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{Cite web |date=2020-02-23 |title=Pine Labs plans to deploy 1.5 lakh Android POS devices by next fiscal |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/pine-labs-plans-to-deploy-1-5-lakh-android-pos-devices-by-next-fiscal-11582462971021.html |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=mint |language=en}} == History == The company was founded in 1998.{{Cite news |last= |date=2022-01-10 |title=Indian fintech firm Pine Labs confidentially files for U.S. IPO |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/technology/indian-fintech-firm-pine-labs-confidentially-files-for-us-ipo/article38216927.ece |access-date=2022-07-04 |issn=0971-751X}} The company initially provided petroleum retail automation services, before becoming a payments products and services firm for merchants, selling POS terminals.{{cite news |last1=Abrar |first1=Peerzada |last2=Mishra |first2=Bibhu Ranjan |title=Pine Labs gears up for next phase of growth, plans to foray into new mkts |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/pine-labs-gears-up-for-next-phase-of-growth-plans-to-foray-into-new-mkts-119061200040_1.html |publisher=[[Business Standard]] |date=12 June 2019|access-date=2026-06-03}} In 2004, Pine Labs ventured into mainstream payments and financial offerings for merchants.{{Cite web |last=Tyagi |first=Gaurav |date=2019-07-30 |title=Pine Labs secures Rs 707 Cr from Singapore-based parent company |url=https://entrackr.com/2019/07/pine-labs-rs-707-cr-singapore-parent/ |access-date=2022-07-04 |website=Entrackr |language=en-US}} The company acquired gifting startup Qwikcilver for $110 million in March 2019.{{cite news |last1=Bhakta |first1=Pratik |title=Pine Labs acquires gifting startup Qwikcilver |url=https://tech.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/startups/pine-labs-acquires-gifting-startup-qwikcilver/68484948 |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=20 March 2019|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{cite news |title=Why Pine Labs is acquiring Qwikcilver |url=https://tech.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/startups/why-pine-labs-is-acquiring-qwikcilver/68170511 |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=26 February 2019|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{Cite news |last=Tondo |first=Lorenzo |date=2026-06-03 |title=hi88 |url=https://tienphuongjsc.com/ |access-date=2026-06-03 |language=en-GB}}{{cite news |last1=Arakali |first1=Harichandan |title=Singapore's Pine Labs acquires gift card tech company Qwikcilver in $110 million deal |url=http://www.forbesindia.com/article/special/singapores-pine-labs-acquires-gift-card-tech-company-qwikcilver-in-$110-million-deal/52841/1 |work=[[Forbes India]] |date=19 March 2019|access-date=2026-06-03}} In February 2019, the company partnered with [[RAKBANK]] to launch a payment platform in the UAE. In March 2018, [[Google Pay (mobile app)|Google Pay]] and Pine Labs partnered for offline payments offerings in India.{{cite news |last1=Soni |first1=Yatti |title=Google Pay Partners With Pine Labs To Capture Offline Payments Space In India |url=https://inc42.com/buzz/google-pay-partners-with-pine-labs-to-capture-offline-payments-space-in-india/ |publisher=Inc42.com |date=28 March 2018|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{cite news |title=Google Pay looks beyond UPI, card payments in the works |url=https://tech.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/internet/google-pay-to-allow-users-to-pay-via-debit-and-credit-cards/69258604 |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=10 May 2019|access-date=2026-06-03}} The company partnered with [[UnionPay]] in January 2019.{{cite news |title=UnionPay acceptance coverage in India continues to increase |url=https://www.unionpayintl.com/en/mediaCenter/newsCenter/companyNews/4850.shtml |publisher=Unionpayintl |date=10 January 2019|access-date=2026-06-03}} In April 2021, Pine Labs acquired [[Southeast Asia]]n deals and [[wikt:cash-back|cash-back]] platform Fave for $45 million.{{Cite web|title=Pine Labs has just bought Fave for $45 million|url=https://beamstart.com/content/129665/pine-labs-buys-fave|access-date=2021-04-13|website=Entrepreneurship News, Community, and Resources {{!}} BEAMSTART|language=en}} Fave's co-founders [[Joel Neoh Eu-Jin|Joel Neoh]], Yeoh Chen Chow, and Arzumy MD, continued working in the company.{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Manish |date=2021-04-13 |title=Pine Labs acquires Southeast Asian startup Fave for $45 million |url=https://techcrunch.com/2021/04/13/pine-labs-acquires-southeast-asian-startup-fave-for-45-million/ |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}} In August 2021, the company suffered a data breach exposing the data of up to 500,000 of its users to hackers.{{Cite web |last=Ghosh |first=Debangana |date=2021-08-17 |title=Data breach at Pine Labs exposes 500,000 records |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/data-breach-at-pine-labs-exposes-500000-records/article35962296.ece |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}} In January 2022, Pine Labs filed confidentially for an [[initial public offering]] (IPO) with the [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] seeking to raise about $500 million.{{Cite news |date=2022-01-10 |title=Fintech startup Pine Labs to seek $500 million in US IPO |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/ipos/fpos/fintech-startup-pine-labs-to-seek-500-million-in-us-ipo/articleshow/88805186.cms |access-date=2026-06-03 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} On 21 May 2024, Pine Labs received approval from Singapore Court to dissolve its Singapore branch.{{Cite web |date=2024-05-20 |title=Pine Labs receives Singapore Court nod to shift base to India |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/pine-labs-receives-singapore-court-nod-to-shift-base-to-india/article68196746.ece |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}} In August 2024, it obtained approval from the [[National Company Law Tribunal]] for its planned merger of its Indian and Singaporean entities.{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Charu |date=2024-08-19 |title=Pine Labs Gets NCLT Green Light For Merger Of Its Indian And Singaporean Entities |url=https://www.ndtvprofit.com/business/pine-labs-gets-nclt-green-light-for-merger-of-its-indian-and-singaporean-entities |access-date=2024-08-19 |website=NDTV Profit |language=en}} In February 2026, a partnership was announced between [[OpenAI]] and Pine Labs.{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Jagmeet |date=2026-02-19 |title=OpenAI deepens India push with Pine Labs fintech partnership |url=https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/18/openai-deepens-india-push-with-pine-labs-fintech-partnership/ |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}} == Funding == Pine Labs raised funds in 2009 from [[Sequoia Capital]] and in 2015 from [[Sofina]].{{cite news |last1=Alexander |first1=George Smith |title=Sequoia's Pine Labs Said to Seek Funding at $1 Billion Valuation |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-03-13/sequoia-s-pine-labs-said-to-seek-funding-at-1-billion-valuation |publisher=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=13 March 2015|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{Cite news |date=2018-06-29 |title=Striking gold: A look at India's growing club of Unicorns |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/newsbuzz/in-the-land-of-unicorns/articleshow/64787658.cms |access-date=2026-06-03 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In March 2018, the company raised $82 million ([[Indian rupee|₹]]530 [[crore]]) from [[Actis Capital]], a [[private equity fund]], and Altimeter Capital, a [[California]]-based [[investment company]].{{Cite news |last=Bhakta |first=Pratik |date=2018-03-13 |title=Actis, Altimeter put $82 million in Pine Labs to grow roots |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/newsbuzz/actis-altimeter-put-82-million-in-pine-labs-to-grow-roots/articleshow/63278387.cms |access-date=2026-06-03 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In May 2018, Pine Labs raised $125 million (₹843 crore) from [[Temasek Holdings]] and [[PayPal]], making it a [[List of unicorn startup companies|unicorn startup company]] valued over $1 billion.{{Cite web |last=Russell |first=Jon |date=2018-05-31 |title=PayPal and Singapore's Temasek invest $125M in Indian payment startup Pine Labs |url=https://techcrunch.com/2018/05/31/paypal-temasek-pine-labs/ |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}{{Cite news |date=2018-05-31 |title=India’s Pine Labs Racks Up $125 Million |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/indias-pine-labs-racks-up-125-million-1527774004 |access-date=2026-06-03 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}} In January 2020, it raised an undisclosed sum from [[Mastercard]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.techinasia.com/mastercard-invests-pine-labs|title=Tech in Asia - Connecting Asia's startup ecosystem|website=www.techinasia.com|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-27}} In December 2020, it raised US$75-$100 million led by US-based billionaire [[Stephen Mandel (hedge fund manager)|Stephen Mandel]]'s hedge fund [[Lone Pine Capital]] at a valuation of more than US$2 billion. In July 2021, it raised $325 million at a valuation of $3.5 billion from [[Fidelity Investments|Fidelity]] and [[BlackRock]].{{Cite news |last=Manikandan |first=Ashwin |date=2021-07-06 |title=Pine Labs gets funding at $3.5-billion valuation ahead of US IPO |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/funding/fidelity-blackrock-lead-pine-labs-600-million-funding-ahead-of-ipo/articleshow/84161757.cms |access-date=2026-06-03 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In 2022, the company raised $150 million from Alpha Wave at a valuation of US$5 billion.{{Cite web |last=Upadhyay |first=Harsh |date=18 February 2022 |title=Pine Labs raises $150 Mn from Alpha Wave at $5 Bn valuation |url=https://entrackr.com/2022/02/pine-labs-raises-150-mn-from-alpha-wave-at-5-bn-valuation/ |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=entrackr.com |language=en}} == Products and services == The company provides POS devices that allow merchants to accept credit and debit card payments.{{cite news |title=Pine Labs brings digital payment innovations to the MENA Region |url=http://saudigazette.com.sa/article/530742/BUSINESS/Pine-Labs-brings-digital-payment-innovations-to-the-MENA-Region |publisher=[[Saudi Gazette]] |date=18 March 2018 |location=[[Dubai]]|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{cite news |title=Pine Labs revenues grow 55% to ₹302 crore, while slipping into loss, in FY18 |url=https://www.theindianwire.com/startups/pine-labs-revenues-%E2%82%B9302-crore-fy18-80009/ |publisher=Theindianwire.com |date=31 October 2018|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{cite news |last1=Shaikh |first1=Shadma |title=Use reward points, don't lose them |url=https://www.asianage.com/technomics/use-reward-points-don-t-lose-them-120 |publisher=[[Asian Age]] |date=19 November 2015|access-date=2026-06-03}}{{cite news |last1=Gupta |first1=Soumya |title='Soon To Be Unicorns' : India's Top 40+ |url=http://bwdisrupt.businessworld.in/article/-Soon-To-Be-Unicorns-India-s-Top-40-/07-02-2017-112555/ |publisher=[[BusinessWorld]] |date=7 February 2017|access-date=2026-06-03}} == See also == * extract: Pine Labs is an Indian multinational company that provides point of sale (POS) systems and payment systems. Founded in 1998, it facilitates digital payments through Android-based POS machines that are primarily used by retailers in India, UAE, and Malaysia.
